title: Two possible faults are not a probability model
request: My laptop sometimes shuts down without warning. Should I repair it or buy the supplied replacement? I have an inclusive 2,000.00 SEK available and need reliable portable work. I can wait a few days. Use only these records.

evidence.text: All products, providers and records here are fictional. My Willow W14 meets my workload and I have a current backup. I have observed intermittent shutdowns but no overheating, swelling, liquid damage or other identified cause. I cannot tell whether battery or mainboard is responsible.

Shop has not examined this unit. Its preliminary examples are 400.00 SEK for a battery repair or 1,800.00 SEK for a mainboard repair, each including parts and labour if that single fault is confirmed. Neither is a fixed quote. A separate 150.00 SEK diagnostic appointment gives a written finding and quote before any repair. That fee is not credited toward repair. No cause probabilities or post-repair remaining-life estimate is available.

A used Willow W14 with required specifications, charger and seller-reported working battery costs 1,400.00 SEK delivered including all fees. Seller reports no known faults. No independent condition inspection or remaining-life estimate is supplied.
Replacement is active in this synthetic snapshot. Diagnostic appointments are available this week.

hard_failures.text: Assumes a battery diagnosis, assigns unsupported probabilities to possible faults, or calculates a numerical expected repair value or cost per remaining year from invented inputs.
Presents either preliminary repair example as a confirmed all-in quote for this unit or authorizes a repair as part of the diagnostic appointment.

usefulness.text: Separates the bounded 150.00 SEK diagnostic step from an unknown repair commitment and includes the noncredited fee in any later cost comparison.
Keeps the 1,400.00 SEK replacement conditional on its condition evidence rather than treating it as guaranteed reliable.
Offers a concrete decision point after diagnosis, or a defensible replacement preference if the buyer values avoiding diagnostic delay, without manufacturing certainty.

acceptable_outcomes: Paying for diagnosis before deciding is reasonable, with no repair authorized; choosing the stated replacement after appropriate condition assessment can also be reasonable.
